mainTopic: The verses of מלכיות, זכרונות and שופרות; who blows the שופר and who says הלל; and not breaking יום טוב rules for a שופר
overview: The גמרא explains which פסוקים may not be used in מלכיות, זכרונות and שופרות on ראש השנה. Verses about punishment of ישראל are left out, but verses about punishment of the nations may be said. A זכרון of a single person is not used, even when it asks for good. רבי יוסי and רבי יהודה then argue about which verses count and how many: 'revisiting' verses, the 'King of glory' passages, and verses that mention תרועה. Next the גמרא explains רבי יוסי's view that the ten פסוקים should end with a תורה verse. It shows he has enough תורה verses of מלכות because he counts שמע ישראל and similar פסוקים. A new משנה says the שופר is blown under the מוסף leader and הלל is led by the שחרית leader. רבי יוחנן explains this comes from a time of persecution, and רבי אבהו explains why ראש השנה has no הלל. Finally, a משנה teaches that יום טוב rules may not be broken to get a שופר, and the גמרא explains why.

steps.title: Example of a Kingship verse of punishment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives an example of a מלכיות verse that speaks of punishment and so is not said on ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: An example of a Kingship verse of punishment is: 'As I live, says the Lord God, surely with a mighty hand, an outstretched arm, and fury poured out, will I be King over you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining the משנה by giving an example of a מלכיות verse that we may not use because it is about punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse really is about God's kingship, so it belongs in the category of מלכיות. But it describes God ruling with anger and fury. That is the kind of verse the משנה called פורענות.

keyTerms.meaning: Verses about God as King, one of the three special sections of ראש השנה מוסף

steps.confusionAlert: The verse is still a real מלכיות verse. It is left out only because of its angry tone, not because it is not about kingship.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Kingship verses, for example:
"As I live, says the Lord [God],
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 20:33. The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording; some versions leave it out.

phrases.english: surely with a mighty hand
and with an outstretched arm and with fury poured out
will I be King over you."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by illustrating the משנה's rule about מלכיות of פורענות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A kingship verse that describes God ruling with fury, such as יחזקאל 20:33, is not used in מלכיות on ראש השנה.

steps.title: Why the verse is excluded even though רב נחמן saw it as hopeful
steps.stepSummary: Although רב נחמן viewed this angry verse as a hopeful wish for redemption, it is still left out because it is said in anger.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even though רב נחמן said, 'Let God be angry with us with any anger like this, as long as He redeems us,' since the verse is phrased in anger, we do not mention anger on ראש השנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a question it expects us to ask: if רב נחמן saw this verse as a good sign, why not say it? It answers that the verse is still worded in anger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן read the verse as a promise: God will rule over us and redeem us, even if it comes with anger. The גמרא accepts that reading but says the deciding factor is the words themselves. On ראש השנה, a day of judgment, we avoid bringing up God's anger at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The head of the year, ראש השנה

steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that on ראש השנה the wording and tone of a verse matter, not only its hopeful message.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: And even though Rav Nachman said:
Any anger like this,
let the Holy One, blessed be He, be angry with us
and let Him redeem us,
since it was said in anger,
mentioning anger on Rosh HaShana
we do not mention.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the example from step 1 against an implied challenge from רב נחמן's positive reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice of יחזקאל 20:33 as a forbidden verse
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב נחמן saw this verse as a hopeful promise of redemption, so maybe it should be allowed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the verse's wording from its underlying message
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the verse carries a hopeful message, it could be said.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because it is phrased in anger, it is not mentioned on ראש השנה.

steps.title: Examples of זכרונות and שופרות verses of punishment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives an example of a זכרונות verse and a שופרות verse that speak of calamity and are not said.
steps.simpleTranslation: A Remembrance verse of punishment is, for example: 'And He remembered that they were flesh.' A שופר verse of punishment is, for example: 'Sound the שופר in גבעה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its list of forbidden examples. It gives one for זכרונות and one for שופרות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The זכרון verse speaks of God remembering how weak and short-lived people are. The שופר verse is a call of alarm about coming danger. Both mention remembering or the shofar in a setting of trouble, so they fit the משנה's category of פורענות.

keyTerms.meaning: Remembrance, the topic of the זכרונות section
Shofar, the topic of the שופרות section
Etc., the rest of the verse

phrases.english: Remembrance, for example:
"And He remembered that they were flesh, etc."
Shofar, for example:
"Sound the shofar in Giva, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of examples begun in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: זכרונות and שופרות verses describing calamity for ישראל are not used on ראש השנה.
steps.whatToRemember: For each of the three sections, a verse about punishment of ישראל is left out, even if it fits the topic.

steps.title: Verses about punishment of the nations are allowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits the משנה: verses of punishment directed at the נכרים may be said.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if one wants to say Kingship, Remembrance, or Shofar verses about the punishment of the nations, he may say them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits the משנה's rule. The ban covers only punishment of ישראל, not punishment of the nations. This sets up the examples in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern was mentioning anger against us on our day of judgment. When the punishment falls on our enemies, it is really part of God's rescue of ישראל. So it is not a problem.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the real reason behind the משנה: the problem is calling up judgment against ישראל, not mentioning punishment in general.

phrases.english: But if he comes to say
Kingship, Remembrance, and Shofar verses
of the punishment of the nations, he may say them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a limit on the rule illustrated in steps 1-3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Verses of מלכיות, זכרונות, and שופרות about punishment of the נכרים may be said.

steps.title: Examples of allowed verses about the nations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives examples of permitted מלכיות, זכרונות, and שופרות verses that describe punishment of the nations.
steps.simpleTranslation: Kingship, for example: 'The Lord reigns, let the peoples tremble,' and 'The Lord is King forever, the nations are lost from His land.' Remembrance, for example: 'Remember, Lord, against the children of אדום.' שופר, for example: 'And the Lord God will sound the שופר and go with storms of the south,' and it says next: 'The Lord of hosts will defend them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the rule from step 4 by giving an allowed example for each of the three sections.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each example shows God's power aimed against our enemies, such as the nations trembling, אדום being remembered for its crimes, or a storm against the enemy. For the שופר verse, the גמרא adds the next verse to show that the שופר here is about protecting ישראל.

phrases.english: Kingship, for example:
"The Lord reigns, let the peoples tremble,"
and for example: "The Lord is King forever and ever,
the nations are lost from His land."
Remembrance, for example:
"Remember, O Lord, against the children of Edom, etc."
Shofar, for example:
"And the Lord God will sound the shofar
and will go with storms of the south,"
and it is written: "The Lord of hosts will defend them."
phrases.notes: This is the very next פסוק. It shows the shofar here is about God protecting ישראל from their enemies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the exception stated in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Verses showing God's kingship, remembrance, or shofar directed against the nations are acceptable.
steps.whatToRemember: Punishment of ישראל: not said. Punishment of our enemies, which brings our rescue: may be said.

steps.title: No verses about remembering an individual
steps.stepSummary: A זכרון verse about a single person is not used, even if it asks for good.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not mention a Remembrance verse about an individual, even if it is for good, such as: 'Remember me, Lord, when You favor Your people,' or 'Remember me, my God, for good.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a new rule for זכרונות. Verses where one person asks to be remembered are not used, even when they ask for something good.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This rule is different from the earlier ones. The issue here is not punishment, because these verses are positive requests. The problem is that they speak of one person rather than the whole people, so they are not fit for the communal זכרונות.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think these verses are excluded for being negative. They are fully positive. The only issue is that they are about a יחיד.

phrases.english: We do not mention a remembrance of an individual,
and even if it is for good,
for example: "Remember me, O Lord, when You favor Your people,"
and for example: "Remember me, my God, for good."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a separate limit on זכרונות, unrelated to the topic of punishment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: זכרונות verses about an individual are not said, even when they request good.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two kinds of verses we leave out: verses about punishment of ישראל, and זכרונות verses about one person, even good ones.

steps.title: Do 'revisiting' verses count as remembrance verses?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says verses using the word פקד ('revisit') count as זכרונות; רבי יהודה says they do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Verses about God 'revisiting' are like remembrance verses. Examples: 'And ה׳ revisited שרה' and 'I have surely revisited you.' This is רבי יוסי's view. רבי יהודה says they are not like remembrance verses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new מחלוקת about whether a verse with the word פקד can be used in the זכרונות section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, the verses discussed used the word 'remember' (זכר). רבי יוסי says 'revisit' (פקד) means the same thing, so these verses count. רבי יהודה says only real זכירה language counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Verses that speak of God 'revisiting' or taking note of someone (from the root פקד)
The remembrance section of ראש השנה מוסף, built from verses about God remembering

phrases.english: Verses of 'revisiting' are like remembrance verses,
for example: 'And ה׳ revisited Sarah,'
and for example: 'I have surely revisited you,'
these are the words of Rabbi Yosei.
Rabbi Yehuda says: They are not like remembrance verses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from which kinds of remembrance verses are excluded to which kinds of wording qualify as remembrance verses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי: verses using פקד count as זכרונות. רבי יהודה: they do not.

steps.title: But שרה's verse is about only one person
steps.stepSummary: Even if פקד verses count, how can רבי יוסי use 'וה׳ פקד את שרה' when a remembrance about one person is not used?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי יוסי: even if 'revisiting' verses are like remembrance verses, 'And ה׳ revisited שרה' is a revisiting of one person!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי's first example, because it seems to break the rule from just before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 taught that a זכרון verse about a single person is not used, even when it is a good remembrance. שרה is one person, so her verse should be ruled out even if we accept that פקד counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted that / even if we accept
A revisiting of an individual (one person)

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Yosei, granted
that 'revisiting' verses are like remembrance verses,

phrases.aramaic: ״וַה׳ פָּקַד אֶת שָׂרָה״ — פִּקָּדוֹן דְּיָחִיד הוּא!
phrases.english: 'And ה׳ revisited Sarah' is a revisiting of an individual!
phrases.notes: This is the rule from just before: a remembrance of one person is not said, even if it is a good one.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי נְהִי נָמֵי דְּפִקְדוֹנוֹת הֲרֵי הֵן כְּזִכְרוֹנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוסי's example from Step 7 using the rule from Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's use of 'וה׳ פקד את שרה' as a זכרונות verse
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A זכרון about a single person is not used (Step 6). שרה is a single person, so the verse should be invalid no matter how we treat the word פקד.

steps.title: שרה counts like many people
steps.stepSummary: Since a whole nation came from שרה, a verse about her counts as being about many.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since many people came from her, she is like many.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: שרה's verse is not really about just one person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שרה is the mother of the Jewish people, and all of כלל ישראל came from that פקידה. So remembering her is like remembering the whole nation, and the rule against verses about one person does not apply.

phrases.english: Since many came from her,
phrases.notes: He means the whole Jewish people, who descend from שרה.

phrases.english: she is like many.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: the individual is treated as a group
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שרה is one person, so her verse is a remembrance of an individual and cannot be used.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the whole nation came from her, her פקידה counts as a remembrance of many, so the verse is valid for רבי יוסי.
steps.whatToRemember: A verse about one person can still count as being about the community if that person is the root of the whole nation, like שרה.

steps.title: How many kingship verses are in 'Lift up your heads, O gates'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי counts the first half of the passage as two מלכיות and the second half as three.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Lift up your heads, O gates, and be lifted up, everlasting doors, so the King of glory may come in. Who is this King of glory? ה׳, strong and mighty, ה׳ mighty in battle. Lift up your heads, O gates, and lift them up, everlasting doors, so the King of glory may come in. Who is this King of glory? ה׳ of hosts, He is the King of glory, Selah.' The first part counts as two, the second as three. These are the words of רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a passage from תהלים and gives רבי יוסי's count of how many מלכיות verses it holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'מלך הכבוד' come up twice in the first half and three times in the second half. רבי יוסי counts every mention, even the question 'Who is the King of glory?', so he gets two and then three.

keyTerms.meaning: The kingship section of ראש השנה מוסף, built from verses about God as King
The first one (first half of the passage)
The second one (second half of the passage)

phrases.english: 'Lift up your heads, O gates,'
and be lifted up, everlasting doors,
so that the King of glory may come in.
Who is this King of glory?

phrases.aramaic: ה׳ עִזּוּז וְגִבּוֹר ה׳ גִּבּוֹר מִלְחָמָה.
phrases.english: ה׳, strong and mighty, ה׳ mighty in battle.
Lift up your heads, O gates,
and lift them up, everlasting doors,
so that the King of glory may come in.
Who then is this King of glory?

phrases.aramaic: ה׳ צְבָאוֹת הוּא מֶלֶךְ הַכָּבוֹד סֶלָה״.
phrases.english: ה׳ of hosts, He is the King of glory, Selah.'
The first part counts as two,
phrases.notes: Count the times 'מלך הכבוד' appears in the first half: twice.

phrases.english: the second part counts as three,
these are the words of Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from זכרונות to a new question about counting מלכיות verses, with the same two תנאים disagreeing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי: the first half of the 'שאו שערים' passage gives two מלכיות, the second half gives three.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's smaller count
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה counts the first half as one מלכיות verse and the second half as two.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: the first part counts as one, the second part as two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי יהודה's side of the מחלוקת, which counts one fewer in each half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה does not count the question 'Who is the King of glory?', since a question is not a statement that ה׳ is King. Taking out one question from each half gives one and two.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
The first part counts as one,
the second part counts as two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side of the מחלוקת begun in Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: the first half gives one מלכיות verse and the second half gives two, because the question 'מי זה מלך הכבוד' is not counted.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי counts every mention of 'מלך הכבוד' (2 and 3). רבי יהודה leaves out the question lines (1 and 2).

steps.title: Does 'Sing praises to our King' count as two kingship verses or one?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי counts תהלים 47:7–8 as two מלכיות verses; רבי יהודה counts it as one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verses 'Sing praises to God, sing praises, sing praises to our King, sing praises. For God is the King of all the earth' count as two kingship verses, according to רבי יוסי. רבי יהודה says they count as only one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another example of the same counting argument from the last two steps. This time it is a pair of פסוקים from תהלים that mention God as King twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The passage calls God King twice: 'our King' and 'King of all the earth.' רבי יוסי counts each mention as its own מלכיות verse, so he gets two. רבי יהודה counts the passage as only one, which fits his stricter counting in Step 11.

keyTerms.meaning: Two / one, meaning how many verses this counts as

phrases.english: "Sing praises to God, sing praises, sing praises to our King, sing praises.
For God is the King of all the earth"
Two — these are the words of Rabbi Yosei.
phrases.notes: He means it counts as two מלכיות verses.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: one.

steps.triggerLanguage: זַמְּרוּ אֱלֹהִים זַמֵּרוּ זַמְּרוּ לְמַלְכֵּנוּ זַמֵּרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another example of the same counting dispute from Steps 10–11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי: two מלכיות verses; רבי יהודה: one.

steps.title: Both agree that 'God reigns over the nations' counts as one verse
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees that תהלים 47:9 counts as only one מלכיות verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: They agree about 'God reigns over the nations, God sits upon His sacred throne' that it counts as one.
steps.whatsHappening: After the argument, the ברייתא points to a verse where רבי יוסי and רבי יהודה agree. This verse counts as only one מלכיות verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This verse also has two halves that mention God. Only the first half uses the word for reigning as King. The second half talks about God's throne but does not call Him King, so even רבי יוסי counts only one.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume רבי יוסי counts every mention of God twice. Here even he counts only one, because only one half uses kingship language.

phrases.english: And they agree about "God reigns over the nations,
God sits upon His sacred throne"
that it counts as one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the counting dispute by naming a verse where both sides agree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone counts תהלים 47:9 as a single מלכיות verse.
steps.whatToRemember: In counting מלכיות verses, רבי יוסי counts more generously than רבי יהודה. Still, both agree that a phrase which does not call God King does not add another verse.

steps.title: A remembrance verse that also mentions תרועה
steps.stepSummary: A זכרון verse that also says תרועה may be said with זכרונות and with שופרות according to רבי יוסי; רבי יהודה allows it only with זכרונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: A remembrance verse that mentions תרועה, like 'A solemn rest, a memorial of blasts, a sacred convocation': one may say it with the זכרונות and also with the שופרות, according to רבי יוסי. רבי יהודה says one says it only with the זכרונות.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא starts a new topic: verses that use the word תרועה. Here the verse also has the word זכרון, so the question is which section or sections it belongs in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי lets one verse serve in two sections: זכרונות, because of the word זכרון, and שופרות, because of the word תרועה. רבי יהודה puts it only in זכרונות. He does not let the word תרועה, without the word שופר, make it a שופרות verse.

keyTerms.meaning: Blast or sounding, the sound of the shofar
The section of shofar verses in מוסף

phrases.english: A remembrance verse that has a mention of sounding in it
for example: "A solemn rest, a memorial of blasts, a sacred convocation"
one says it with the remembrance verses

phrases.aramaic: וְאוֹמְרָהּ עִם הַשּׁוֹפָרוֹת, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי.
phrases.english: and says it with the shofar verses — these are the words of Rabbi Yosei.
Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ אוֹמְרָהּ אֶלָּא עִם הַזִּכְרוֹנוֹת בִּלְבָד.
phrases.english: one says it only with the remembrance verses alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from counting verses to sorting verses that mention תרועה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי: the verse goes in both זכרונות and שופרות; רבי יהודה: only in זכרונות.

steps.title: A kingship verse that also mentions תרועה
steps.stepSummary: A מלכות verse that also says תרועה may be said with מלכיות and with שופרות according to רבי יוסי; רבי יהודה allows it only with מלכיות.
steps.simpleTranslation: A kingship verse that mentions תרועה, like 'The Lord his God is with him, and the sounding of a king is among them': one may say it with the מלכיות and also with the שופרות, according to רבי יוסי. רבי יהודה says one says it only with the מלכיות.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the same pattern as the last step, now with a kingship verse instead of a remembrance verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again רבי יוסי lets the verse serve in two sections: מלכיות, because of the word מלך, and שופרות, because of the word תרועה. רבי יהודה keeps it in מלכיות only. His view stays the same: the word תרועה alone does not make a verse a שופרות verse.

keyTerms.meaning: Kingship, a verse about God as King
The section of kingship verses in מוסף

phrases.english: A kingship verse that has a mention of sounding with it

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן: ״ה׳ אֱלֹהָיו עִמּוֹ וּתְרוּעַת מֶלֶךְ בּוֹ״
phrases.english: for example: "The Lord his God is with him, and the sounding of a king is among them"
one says it with the kingship verses

phrases.aramaic: וְאוֹמְרָהּ עִם הַשּׁוֹפָרוֹת, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי.
phrases.english: and says it with the shofar verses — these are the words of Rabbi Yosei.
Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ אוֹמְרָהּ אֶלָּא עִם הַמַּלְכִיּוֹת בִּלְבָד.
phrases.english: one says it only with the kingship verses alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the pattern of Step 14 for a kingship verse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי: the verse goes in both מלכיות and שופרות; רבי יהודה: only in מלכיות.

steps.title: A verse that mentions only תרועה and nothing else
steps.stepSummary: A verse with only the word תרועה is said with שופרות according to רבי יוסי; רבי יהודה says it is not said at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: A verse that mentions תרועה and nothing else, like 'It shall be a day of sounding for you': one says it with the שופרות, according to רבי יוסי. רבי יהודה says one does not say it at all.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last case in the list: a verse that has the word תרועה but no word for remembrance or kingship. The question is whether it may be used at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי, the word תרועה is enough to make this a שופרות verse. For רבי יהודה, תרועה without the word שופר is not a שופרות verse. The verse also does not fit מלכיות or זכרונות, so he leaves it out completely.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three תרועה cases. With זכרון or מלכות in the verse, רבי יוסי uses it in two sections and רבי יהודה in one. With nothing else in the verse, רבי יוסי uses it for שופרות and רבי יהודה does not use it at all. The difference is whether the word תרועה, without the word שופר, is enough for a שופרות verse.

phrases.english: A mention of sounding that has nothing else with it
for example: "It shall be a day of sounding for you"

phrases.aramaic: אוֹמְרָהּ עִם הַשּׁוֹפָרוֹת, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי.
phrases.english: one says it with the shofar verses — these are the words of Rabbi Yosei.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
one does not say it at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the three-case list of verses that mention תרועה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי: the verse goes in שופרות; רבי יהודה: it is not said at all.

steps.title: The משנה: begin with the תורה and end with a נביא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: the ten פסוקים begin with the תורה and end with the נביאים. רבי יוסי says ending with the תורה also works.
steps.simpleTranslation: One begins with the תורה and ends with a נביא. רבי יוסי says: if he ended with the תורה, he has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה about the order of the פסוקים. This sets up a close reading of רבי יוסי's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא gives one order: open with תורה verses and close with a verse from the נביאים. רבי יוסי adds that closing with a תורה verse is also valid. The exact wording 'אם השלים' will be examined in the next step.

phrases.english: One begins with the Torah and concludes with a Prophet,
phrases.notes: This is about the ten פסוקים said for each of מלכיות, זכרונות and שופרות.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
If he concluded with the Torah, he has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from which verses count to the order of the verses, quoting a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Begin with the תורה and end with a נביא; רבי יוסי says ending with the תורה also works.

steps.title: Reading רבי יוסי's words as 'only after the fact'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads 'אם השלים' to mean ending with the תורה is valid only after the fact, not the plan from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If he concluded' means: after the fact, yes; from the start, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a close inference from רבי יוסי's wording. This is setting up a challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אם' ('if') suggests something you did, not something you should plan to do. So רבי יוסי seems to allow ending with the תורה only בדיעבד.

keyTerms.meaning: after the fact, once it was already done
from the start, as the plan

phrases.english: "If he concluded":
After the fact, yes; from the start, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם הִשְׁלִים דִּיעֲבַד אִין לְכַתְּחִילָּה לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads the exact wording of רבי יוסי from step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the wording alone, רבי יוסי allows ending with the תורה only בדיעבד.

steps.title: A ברייתא says ending with the תורה is praiseworthy
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יוסי calling one who ends with the תורה praiseworthy, which sounds like the best way from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: רבי יוסי says, one who ends with the תורה is praiseworthy!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reading from step 18 using a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You would not call something 'praiseworthy' if it were only acceptable after the fact. So in the ברייתא, רבי יוסי seems to prefer ending with the תורה from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: but it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: Rabbi Yosei says:
One who concludes with the Torah is praiseworthy!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the inference of step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that רבי יוסי allows ending with the תורה only בדיעבד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Calling it 'praiseworthy' shows it is preferred from the start, which clashes with 'only after the fact.'

steps.title: Read the משנה as 'he concludes'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by changing the reading of the משנה from 'if he concluded' to 'he concludes.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: 'he concludes.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by rereading רבי יוסי's words in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה says 'משלים' ('he concludes'), it states the plan from the start, matching the ברייתא. The 'only after the fact' reading goes away.

phrases.english: Say: "He concludes."
phrases.notes: Instead of 'if he concluded,' read רבי יוסי as saying 'one concludes with the תורה.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי allows ending with the תורה only after the fact.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי says to end with the תורה from the start.

steps.title: But the משנה clearly says 'if he concluded'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the משנה really says 'if he concluded,' which still sounds like only after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it teaches 'if he concluded': after the fact, yes; from the start, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer, since you cannot just ignore the words in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אם' is in the משנה, so saying 'read it as משלים' seems to clash with the text. The 'after the fact' inference comes back.

phrases.english: But it teaches "if he concluded":
After the fact, yes; from the start, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 20.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה actually says 'אם השלים,' and that wording points to בדיעבד only.

steps.title: Rereading the whole משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the משנה: רבי יוסי says to end with the תורה, and 'אם השלים' refers to ending with a נביא, which is valid after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: One begins with the תורה and ends with a נביא. רבי יוסי says: one ends with the תורה, and if he ended with a נביא, he has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by spelling out what the משנה is really saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now both the 'משלים' and the 'אם השלים' fit. רבי יוסי's plan from the start is to end with the תורה, and the 'if' part is about ending with a נביא, which still works after the fact. This matches the ברייתא that calls ending with the תורה praiseworthy.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what it is saying

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוסי, the best way is to end with a תורה verse; ending with a נביא verse still works after the fact.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
One begins with the Torah and concludes with a Prophet.
Rabbi Yosei says: One concludes with the Torah,
and if he concluded with a Prophet, he has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the משנה as shortened wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אם השלים' refers to ending with the תורה, so it is only בדיעבד.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אם השלים' refers to ending with a נביא; ending with the תורה is the plan from the start.

steps.title: The ותיקין used to end with the תורה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports this: רבי אלעזר son of רבי יוסי says the ותיקין used to end with the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is also taught so: רבי אלעזר son of רבי יוסי said: the ותיקין would end it with the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports the conclusion of step 22.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Careful, pious people did this as their regular practice, so ending with the תורה is a preferred way, not just a fallback. It comes from רבי יוסי's own son, which fits his father's view.

keyTerms.meaning: it was also taught this way (support)
careful, pious people who keep מצוות in the best way

phrases.english: It is also taught so:
Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Yosei, said:
The pious ones would conclude it with the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the reading of step 22.
steps.raayaObject: That ending with the תורה is preferred from the start according to רבי יוסי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי אלעזר בר רבי יוסי about the practice of the ותיקין.

steps.title: מלכיות doesn't have enough תורה verses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: זכרונות and שופרות have many תורה verses, but מלכיות has only three, which is not enough for רבי יוסי's order.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works for זכרונות and שופרות, since there are many verses. But for מלכיות there are only three: 'ה׳ his God is with him, and the sound of a king is among them'; 'And He was king in ישורון'; 'ה׳ will reign forever and ever.' We need ten, and there are not enough!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem with רבי יוסי's view: for מלכיות, there seem to be too few תורה verses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you open with three תורה verses and also close with a תורה verse, you need four תורה verses for מלכיות. The תורה only has three clear מלכות verses. So רבי יוסי's preferred order seems impossible for מלכיות.

keyTerms.meaning: it makes sense for (this case, but not the other)

phrases.english: Granted, for Remembrances and Shofarot there are many;
but for Kingship, there are only three:
"The Lord his God is with him, and the sounding of a king is among them,"
"And He was king in Jeshurun,"
"The Lord shall reign forever and ever,"
and we need ten, and there aren't enough!
phrases.notes: For רבי יוסי, the first three and the last of the ten come from the תורה, so that takes four תורה verses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the practical workability of the conclusion in steps 22–23.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's rule to end with a תורה verse, as applied to מלכיות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His order needs four תורה מלכות verses, but only three exist.

steps.title: רבי יוסי counts שמע ישראל as a מלכות verse
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא brings a source: רבי יוסי counts שמע ישראל as a מלכות verse, while רבי יהודה does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: Come and hear: 'Hear, O ישראל, ה׳ is our God, ה׳ is one' is a מלכות verse; these are the words of רבי יוסי. רבי יהודה says: it is not a מלכות verse.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא begins answering the problem from step 24 by bringing a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי, שמע ישראל counts as a fourth תורה מלכות verse, so he does have enough verses for his order. רבי יהודה does not count it. This fits steps 12–16, where רבי יוסי counts verses more generously than רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: come and hear (a source is being brought)

phrases.english: Rav Huna said: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: ״שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ ה׳ אֶחָד״ — מַלְכוּת,
phrases.english: "Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is one" is Kingship,
these are the words of Rabbi Yosei.
Rabbi Yehuda says: It is not Kingship.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24 by bringing a source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Bringing a source that adds a fourth תורה מלכות verse for רבי יוסי
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תורה has only three מלכות verses, so רבי יוסי's order cannot work for מלכיות.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי counts שמע ישראל as מלכות, which gives him a fourth תורה verse.

steps.title: More verses רבי יוסי counts as Kingship
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: two more פסוקים about ה׳ being the only God are counted as מלכות by רבי יוסי, but not by רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Know this day and take it to heart that ה׳ is God, there is none else" is a Kingship verse, says רבי יוסי. רבי יהודה says it is not. "You were shown, so that you would know that ה׳ is God, there is none besides Him" is a Kingship verse, says רבי יוסי. רבי יהודה says it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the source רב הונא brought. It lists two more פסוקים from the תורה that רבי יוסי counts as מלכות verses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 24 the problem was that the תורה seemed to have only three מלכות verses, which is not enough for רבי יוסי's order. Because רבי יוסי also counts these two פסוקים (along with שמע ישראל), he has enough. He can start with תורה verses and also end with a תורה verse. רבי יהודה does not count them as מלכות verses.

keyTerms.meaning: A verse about ה׳'s Kingship, used in the מלכיות blessing of מוסף
These are the words of רבי יוסי

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יוסי, פסוקים that declare ה׳ is the only God count as Kingship verses. That gives him enough תורה verses for מלכיות.

phrases.english: "Know this day and take it to your heart

phrases.aramaic: כִּי ה׳ הוּא הָאֱלֹהִים אֵין עוֹד״
phrases.english: that ה׳ is God, there is none else"
is a Kingship verse; these are the words of רבי יוסי.
רבי יהודה says: It is not a Kingship verse.
"You were shown, so that you would know

phrases.aramaic: כִּי ה׳ הוּא הָאֱלֹהִים אֵין עוֹד מִלְבַדּוֹ״
phrases.english: that ה׳ is God, there is none besides Him"
is a Kingship verse; these are the words of רבי יוסי.
רבי יהודה says: It is not a Kingship verse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted by רב הונא in step 25.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוסי has enough תורה verses of מלכות for his order
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא quoted by רב הונא listing more פסוקים רבי יוסי counts as מלכות

steps.title: משנה: the second leader handles the שופר, the first leads הלל
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: on ראש השנה the second חזן (מוסף) is in charge of the שופר blowing, and on days with הלל the first חזן (שחרית) leads הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: On ראש השנה, the second person who leads the davening is the one who has the שופר blown. On days when הלל is said, the first leader is the one who says הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It tells us which שליח ציבור handles the שופר and which one leads הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two leaders: one for שחרית (the first) and one for מוסף (the second). The שופר goes with the second leader. הלל goes with the first leader. The משנה does not give reasons, so the גמרא will ask why.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who goes before the ark, meaning the חזן
Has the שופר blown (is in charge of the blowing)
The praise chapters of תהלים said on יום טוב

phrases.english: משנה:
The one who goes before the ark to lead
on the יום טוב of ראש השנה:
the second one has the שופר blown.
phrases.notes: The second leader is the one who leads מוסף.

phrases.english: And at a time when הלל is said,
the first one leads the הלל.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הָעוֹבֵר לִפְנֵי הַתֵּיבָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the previous discussion of מלכיות ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שופר is blown under the second (מוסף) leader, and הלל is led by the first (שחרית) leader.

steps.title: Why does the second leader do the שופר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the שופר goes with the second leader, and suggests a reason: more people are present by then.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is the second leader the one who has the שופר blown? Is it because "the King's glory is in a big crowd"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the משנה's rule about the שופר and suggests one. This sets up a challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By מוסף, more people have arrived in shul. Doing the שופר in front of a bigger crowd shows more honor to ה׳. That is the idea of ברוב עם הדרת מלך.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Why this case?
In a big crowd is the King's glory (a מצוה done with more people honors ה׳ more)

phrases.english: גמרא:
What is different that the second one has the שופר blown?
Is it because "in a big crowd is the King's glory"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the משנה's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the שופר is assigned to the second leader

steps.title: Then הלל should also go to the second leader
steps.stepSummary: If a bigger crowd is the reason, then הלל should also be moved to the second leader.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, הלל should also be said by the second leader, because of "in a big crowd is the King's glory."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the suggested reason. If a bigger crowd matters, that should be true for הלל too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason of ברוב עם הדרת מלך would apply to any מצוה, including הלל. But the משנה puts הלל with the first leader. So this reason cannot fully explain the משנה.

phrases.english: If so, הלל too
should be said by the second leader,
because "in a big crowd is the King's glory"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason suggested in step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason ברוב עם הדרת מלך as the explanation for the שופר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reason should apply equally to הלל, yet the משנה gives הלל to the first leader.

steps.title: Maybe Hallel is first because of doing מצוות early
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries the opposite angle: הלל is said by the first leader because eager people do מצוות as early as they can.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, why is הלל said by the first leader? Because eager people do מצוות early.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a different approach. It explains the הלל rule with the idea that we rush to do מצוות early.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the reasoning starts from הלל. Saying it at שחרית means doing the מצוה at the earliest chance, which is the idea of זריזין מקדימין למצוות. The next step will test whether this reason also works for the שופר.

keyTerms.meaning: Eager people do מצוות as early as possible

phrases.english: Rather: what is different about הלל that it is said by the first leader?
Because eager people do מצוות early.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first reason failed, the גמרא tries reasoning from הלל instead.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the reasoning with a different principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The order is set by the size of the crowd
steps.terutzMaskana: Maybe the order is set by doing מצוות early
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why הלל is assigned to the first leader, tried this time through the idea of זריזין מקדימין למצוות

steps.title: Then the שופר should also go to the first leader
steps.stepSummary: If doing מצוות early is the reason, then the שופר should also be blown by the first leader.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then the שופר blowing should also be done by the first leader, because eager people do מצוות early!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the second reason as well. Doing מצוות early should apply to the שופר too. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each reason fits one מצוה but argues against the other. A bigger crowd would put both at מוסף, and rushing to do מצוות would put both at שחרית. So the גמרא still needs to explain why the שופר and הלל are treated differently.
steps.confusionAlert: Neither reason has been rejected as untrue. The problem is only that each one seems to point both מצוות the same way, while the משנה splits them.

phrases.english: Then let us also do the שופר blowing with the first leader,
because eager people do מצוות early!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason offered in step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason זריזין מקדימין למצוות as the explanation for הלל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reason should apply equally to the שופר, yet the משנה gives the שופר to the second leader.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: The Rule Comes From a Time of Persecution
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the שופר was moved to the second leader because of a time of persecution, not because of crowd size.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: They taught this rule in a time of persecution.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finally answers the question of why the שופר goes with מוסף: it began during a time of שמד (persecution).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both earlier reasons failed. 'More people' should have moved הלל too, and 'do מצוות early' should have kept the שופר at שחרית. רבי יוחנן says the real reason is historical. Blowing early was dangerous during the decree, so it was pushed to מוסף, while הלל stayed early because the eager do מצוות as soon as they can.

keyTerms.meaning: A time of religious persecution, when the authorities banned Jewish practice
They taught (this rule of the משנה)

steps.whatToRemember: The שופר is blown at מוסף because of an old persecution. הלל is said at שחרית because eager people do מצוות early.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the שופר blowing is tied to מוסף rather than שחרית, an arrangement that started from a historical danger.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
They taught this in a time of persecution.
phrases.notes: The idea is that during the decree, blowing early was dangerous, so the blowing was pushed later, to מוסף.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בִּשְׁעַת הַשְּׁמָד שָׁנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא of step 31, and through it the whole cycle from steps 28 to 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a new historical reason that explains why the שופר and הלל are treated differently.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the reason had to be a general principle, such as crowd size or doing מצוות early, that would apply to both שופר and הלל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The שופר was moved because of a specific persecution. הלל was never affected, so it stays early under the principle of doing מצוות early.

steps.title: Inference: No הלל on ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה's wording 'at the time of הלל,' the גמרא infers that ראש השנה has no הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the משנה says 'at the time of הלל,' we can infer that on ראש השנה there is no הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads closely into the wording of the משנה and draws a new fact: ראש השנה has no הלל. This sets up the next question, which asks why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה mentioned שופר for ראש השנה and הלל for 'days of הלל' as two separate cases. That suggests the two never happen on the same day. So ראש השנה, the שופר day, is not a הלל day.

keyTerms.meaning: From the fact that it says

phrases.english: From the fact that it says "at the time of הלל,"
phrases.notes: This is quoting our משנה from step 27, which spoke of days when הלל is said.

phrases.english: we can infer that on ראש השנה
there is no הלל.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּקָאָמַר ״בִּשְׁעַת הַלֵּל״, מִכְּלַל דִּבְרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לֵיכָּא הַלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new point drawn from the wording of the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no הלל on ראש השנה.

steps.title: Why Is There No הלל on ראש השנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason that ראש השנה has no הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why ראש השנה, a יום טוב, has no הלל. This is a setup line, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Other holidays have הלל, so leaving it out on ראש השנה needs an explanation. This is a real request for a reason, not an attack on the משנה.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the inference made in step 33.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why הלל is not said on ראש השנה.

steps.title: A Day of Judgment Is Not a Time for Song
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו tells how the angels asked הקב״ה why there is no song on ראש השנה and יום כיפור, and He answered that it is a time of judgment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: The angels asked ה׳, 'Why don't the Jewish people sing before You on ראש השנה and יום כיפור?' He answered: 'Can it be that the King sits on the throne of judgment, with the books of life and death open before Him, and the Jewish people sing?!'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the question with a conversation between the angels and הקב״ה. ראש השנה and יום כיפור are days of judgment, so joyous הלל does not fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הלל is a song of joy and praise. On days when everyone's life is being judged, the right mood is serious and awed. That is why these days have no הלל, even though they are holy days.

keyTerms.meaning: Books of life and books of death

steps.whatToRemember: ראש השנה and יום כיפור have no הלל because they are days of judgment, when joyous song does not fit.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for why we do not say הלל on ראש השנה and יום כיפור.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu said:
The ministering angels said
before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the world!
For what reason do the Jewish people not
say song before You
on Rosh HaShanah and on Yom Kippur?
He said to them:

phrases.aramaic: אֶפְשָׁר מֶלֶךְ יוֹשֵׁב עַל כִּסֵּא דִין,
phrases.english: Is it possible that the King sits on the throne of judgment,
and the books of life and the books of death
are open before Him,
and the Jewish people would be saying song?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: אָמְרוּ מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 34.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There is no הלל on ראש השנה and יום כיפור because they are days of judgment, when joyous song is out of place.

steps.title: New משנה: יום טוב Rules Are Not Broken to Get a שופר
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that one may not break יום טוב prohibitions, whether rabbinic or Torah, in order to get or prepare a שופר, but one may put water or wine in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the שופר of ראש השנה, one may not walk past the תחום, clear a rubble pile, climb a tree, ride an animal, or swim to get it. One may not cut it into shape, whether with something forbidden by the Rabbis or by the Torah. But if one wants to put water or wine into it, he may.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that the מצוה of שופר does not allow breaking יום טוב rules to obtain or prepare one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list covers both rabbinic prohibitions (שבות), such as climbing, riding and swimming, and Torah prohibitions (לא תעשה), such as cutting with real מלאכה. Even a small rabbinic rule is not pushed aside for the שופר. Putting water or wine inside to clear the sound is allowed, because it is not a forbidden act.

keyTerms.meaning: The boundary one may not walk past on שבת or יום טוב
Clearing away a pile of rubble
A rabbinic prohibition on שבת or יום טוב
Our משנה (marks the start of a new משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the שופר is less important here. The משנה is only saying that this מצוה does not override יום טוב prohibitions. The obligation to blow remains in full force.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: The shofar of Rosh HaShanah:
one may not pass the boundary for it,
phrases.notes: The תחום is the limit you may walk outside the town on שבת and יום טוב.

phrases.english: and one may not clear away a pile of rubble for it.
One may not climb a tree,
nor ride on an animal,
nor swim across the water,
and one may not cut it,
whether with something forbidden as a rabbinic rule,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵין בְּדָבָר שֶׁהוּא מִשּׁוּם לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה.
phrases.english: or with something forbidden by a Torah prohibition.
But if he wants
to put water or wine into it,
he may put it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ שׁוֹפָר שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה אֵין מַעֲבִירִין עָלָיו אֶת הַתְּחוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Neither rabbinic nor Torah יום טוב prohibitions may be broken to obtain or prepare a שופר, but putting water or wine into it is permitted.

steps.title: Children May Practice; Blowing Without Intent Does Not Count
steps.stepSummary: The משנה allows children to blow and be taught on ראש השנה, and rules that someone blowing without intent does not fulfill the מצוה, nor does someone who hears him.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not stop children from blowing; rather, we work with them until they learn. One who blows without intent has not fulfilled his obligation, and one who hears from such a person has not fulfilled his obligation either.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with two rules. Children may practice blowing on ראש השנה, and blowing without intending the מצוה does not count, either for the blower or for the listener.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Children are allowed, and even helped, to blow so they will learn the מצוה. A מתעסק blows without meaning to do the מצוה, such as someone just practicing or fooling around. His blowing does not count, and since his blowing is not a מצוה, a listener cannot fulfill the מצוה through it either.

keyTerms.meaning: One who acts without intending the מצוה
He has not fulfilled his obligation

steps.confusionAlert: The same root, עסק, appears twice with different meanings. מתעסקין עמהן means 'working with' children to teach them, while המתעסק means someone who blows without intending the מצוה.
steps.whatToRemember: Children may practice blowing on ראש השנה. Someone who blows without intent does not fulfill the מצוה, and neither does anyone listening to him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה is a key source for the idea that a מצוה needs intent, a theme the גמרא develops elsewhere.

phrases.english: One does not prevent the children from blowing,
rather, one works with them until they learn.
And one who acts without intent has not fulfilled his obligation,
and one who hears from the one acting without intent has not fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with new rules about who may blow and what counts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Children may practice blowing on ראש השנה. Blowing without intent does not fulfill the מצוה, for the blower or for the listener.

steps.title: Why can't שופר override יום טוב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason that one may not break יום טוב prohibitions to get a שופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה by asking why we may not break יום טוב laws for the sake of שופר. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a well-known rule that a positive מצוה (עשה) pushes aside a negative prohibition (לא תעשה). Blowing שופר is an עשה, so we might expect it to override the work prohibitions of יום טוב. The גמרא wants to know why that rule doesn't apply here.

keyTerms.meaning: A positive מצוה pushes aside a negative prohibition (the rule behind the question)

phrases.english: גמרא: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה's ruling (step 36) that יום טוב laws may not be broken for a שופר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the עשה of שופר does not override the יום טוב prohibitions, given the rule עשה דוחה לא תעשה.

steps.title: יום טוב has both an עשה and a לא תעשה
steps.stepSummary: שופר is only an עשה, while יום טוב is both an עשה and a לא תעשה, and an עשה cannot push aside both together.
steps.simpleTranslation: שופר is a positive מצוה, but יום טוב is both a positive מצוה and a prohibition, and a positive מצוה does not push aside a prohibition together with a positive מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that שופר is only one עשה, but working on יום טוב breaks both an עשה and a לא תעשה. One עשה is not strong enough to push aside both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule עשה דוחה לא תעשה only works when the prohibition stands alone. On יום טוב, doing מלאכה breaks the לא תעשה against work and also the עשה to rest. When a prohibition comes together with an עשה, a single עשה like שופר cannot override them.

keyTerms.meaning: A positive מצוה, something you must do
A negative prohibition, something you must not do

keyTerms.term: אֵין עֲשֵׂה דּוֹחֶה אֶת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה וַעֲשֵׂה
keyTerms.meaning: A positive מצוה does not push aside a prohibition that is joined with a positive מצוה

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule used all over ש״ס: an עשה can override a plain לא תעשה, but not a לא תעשה that comes together with an עשה.

phrases.english: Shofar is a positive מצוה,
but a Festival is a positive מצוה and a prohibition —
and a positive מצוה does not override
a prohibition together with a positive מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 38.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יום טוב carries both an עשה and a לא תעשה, and a single עשה (שופר) cannot override both together.
steps.whatToRemember: שופר cannot override יום טוב because יום טוב is an עשה plus a לא תעשה, and one עשה can't push aside both.

steps.title: Why list Torah prohibitions after rabbinic ones?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה and asks: if even rabbinic prohibitions may not be broken for a שופר, why must the משנה say that Torah prohibitions may not be broken?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One may not climb a tree, nor ride on an animal, etc.' Now that you said even rabbinic prohibitions are not allowed, is it necessary to say Torah prohibitions are not allowed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's list and points out that its order seems backward. Once you forbid even the lighter rabbinic prohibitions, the heavier Torah ones are obviously forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה first lists rabbinic-level actions, like climbing a tree or riding an animal, and then also forbids Torah-level actions. Normally, if the lighter thing is forbidden, the heavier one is forbidden too, so mentioning it seems extra. The גמרא is challenging the way the משנה is worded, not the ruling itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Now (that), used to say: since the lighter case is already true

phrases.english: One may not climb a tree

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא רוֹכְבִין עַל גַּבֵּי בְּהֵמָה וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: nor ride on an animal, etc.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the משנה; 'etc.' means the rest of the list there, which ends with Torah-level prohibitions.

phrases.english: Now that you said rabbinic prohibitions are not allowed,
is it necessary to say Torah prohibitions are not?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא דְּרַבָּנַן אָמְרַתְּ לָא, דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא מִיבַּעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new point: the wording and order of the משנה's list from step 36.
steps.kashyaTarget: The order of the משנה, which forbids rabbinic prohibitions and then adds Torah prohibitions.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the lighter rabbinic prohibitions are forbidden, the heavier Torah prohibitions are forbidden all the more, so stating them seems unnecessary.

steps.title: 'This, and no need to say that'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה uses the style of teaching one case and then adding the obvious one.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches in the style of: 'This, and there is no need to say that.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is written in a common style: it states the surprising case, and then adds the obvious case as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה isn't adding the Torah prohibitions as a new teaching. It is saying: rabbinic prohibitions are forbidden, and of course Torah ones are too. This style explains why the extra case appears without making the משנה wasteful.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This, and there is no need to say that': a style that states the new case and then the obvious one

steps.whatToRemember: When a משנה lists an obvious case after a surprising one, it may be using the style זוֹ וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר זוֹ.

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר זוֹ קָתָנֵי.
phrases.english: It teaches: this, and there is no need to say that.

steps.triggerLanguage: זוֹ וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר זוֹ קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 40.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Stylistic explanation of the משנה's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Listing Torah prohibitions after rabbinic ones seems unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה deliberately uses the 'this, and certainly that' style, stating the obvious case after the surprising one.
